s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Osteolysis of the mastoids, semicircular canals, and external auditory canal on CT
Profound right-sided hearing loss on brainstem evoked response audiometry
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Presented to the emergency department with progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls
Initial fall resulted in a nasal bridge laceration
Alert and afebrile on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed intact left tympanic membrane and occluded right external canal
Frenzel’s examination showed no nystagmus
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis and adenoid hypertrophy
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

differentials: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with temporal bone metastasis
per_call: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with temporal bone metastasis

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals, along with a separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Langerhans cell histiocytosis, the presence of osteolytic lesions and otologic abnormalities make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: The occluded right external canal with polypoid tissue and purulent secretion, along with the history of ear problems, make this a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis of the temporal bone
shortlist.why_kept: The contrast-enhanced CT showing bilateral osteolysis and the history of ear problems suggest this as a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Gorham-Stout disease
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of osteolytic lesions and the involvement of the temporal bone and mastoids make this a rare but possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive unsteadiness, recurrent falls, and bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, semicircular canals, and temporal bones, along with a history of ear problems and profound right-sided hearing loss, is most consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which can cause lytic bone lesions and affect multiple systems.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: While eosinophilic granuloma is a form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, it typically presents with solitary bone lesions, which does not fully explain the bilateral and multifocal nature of the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: Cholesteatoma could explain some of the ear symptoms and findings, but it does not account for the systemic nature of the disease, including the osteolytic lesions in the mastoids and the dorsal left parietal bone.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis of the temporal bone
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis could cause some of the bone and ear findings, but it typically presents with signs of infection such as fever, which is not present in this case, and does not fully explain the extent of osteolysis and the specific pattern of hearing loss.

rejected.label: Gorham-Stout disease
rejected.why: Gorham-Stout disease is characterized by progressive osteolysis, but it typically involves more widespread bone destruction and does not specifically explain the ear symptoms and the pattern of hearing loss seen in this patient.
